newsitem.title: GERMANY: German oilseeds lobby hostile to EU reform plans.
newsitem.headline: German oilseeds lobby hostile to EU reform plans.

text.p: Germany's oilseed lobby, the Union for the Promotion of Oil and Protein Crops (UFOP) is concerned new European Commission draft plans on area aid payments may threaten oilseeds output, managing director Hans-Juergen Bertram said.
"We think paying a single area aid payment for both grains and oilseeds would be unacceptable because it would lead to a reduction in oilseeds," he said in a telephone interview.
"Grain yields are naturally higher and oilseeds would not be financially competitive if the plans were put into practice."
The draft had not been circulated across the EU and UFOP was due to draw up a strategy to combat the proposal at a meeting on Wednesday, he said.
The proposal is part of a farm reform package which will be presented to the EU Parliament by Commission President Jacques Santer in Strasbourg on Wednesday.
Bertram said wheat and maize would benefit from the plans which entail choosing a base of 66 Ecus a tonne multiplied by regional cereals reference yields fixed in 1992.
This would bring gains in cereals aid (from 54 Ecus formerly) but cuts of more than a third in oilseeds aid.
Bertram said this did not make sense at a time when demand for oilseeds was growing worldwide while grain production was in balance and could easily move into surplus.
The plan was probably motivated by a desire to free the EU from restrictions on its subsidised oilseed area under a bilateral deal with the United States, the so-called Blair House accord, he said.
But the Commission's approach ignored the fact that commercial conditions for growing oilseeds in the EU were far less favourable than in the U.S., the world's leading producer.
"We in the EU haven't got the large farm structures and we need a certain amount of oilseeds on our land to avoid monocultures," Bertram said.
Crop rotation helps cut fertiliser and pesticide use and combats soil erosion.
Traders said rapeseed and sunflowerseed prices in the EU could rise sharply if the Commission's plans were implemented.
